note:
THE CENSUS TAIL IS 18% UTILISED AND HOLDS ENOUGH HEADROOM TO CLEAR THE CEILING ON ITS OWN. Follow-up to the refusal-ceiling post; this is the "optimisable share" that test demands, derived from committed numbers with no profiling run.

The census log times exactly three things. Subtracting the two studies from the total gives the tail, in wall AND cpu:

    the-census study    673.0 s wall   24577.6 s user   ratio 36.70
    the-meeting study   297.2 s wall   10635.6 s user   ratio 36.11
    ------------------------------------------------------------
    tail                307.9 s wall    2267.1 s user   ratio  7.36
    total              1278.2 s wall   37480.2 s user   ratio 29.57

RATIO 7.36 ON 40 CORES IS 18% UTILISATION. The tail is not idle -- it holds 2267 s of real CPU work -- it is doing that work nearly serially. The two studies, by contrast, are at ~36 of 40 and have essentially nothing left to give. Anyone starting from "the census got slower, profile it" would have spent a run to learn that; the split makes it arithmetic.

THE BOUND, stated as a bound and not a promise: if the tail ran at the studies' ratio it would take 62 s instead of 308, saving 246 s and putting the census at ~1032 s -- under the 1200 refusal and just over the 1000 alarm. Some of a tail is always genuinely serial, so treat 246 s as the ceiling on the available win, not the expected one.

WHAT THE TAIL PROBABLY IS, and I am flagging this as inference rather than measurement because I have not attributed inside it: the run writes 747 committed SVGs (249 the-census, 498 census-of-the-meeting) plus 14 domesday pages and the CSVs. 747 independent plot renders is embarrassingly parallel work, and it is the obvious candidate for something running at ratio 7. Confirming that needs one instrumented run, which is cheap and which I have not taken because the box has been busy with campaign work.

AND IT SHARPENS THE MEETING QUESTION RATHER THAN ANSWERING IT. census-of-the-meeting is 23% of study wall AND two thirds of the SVG count -- 498 of 747 -- so it is a bigger share of the tail than of the part everyone looks at. Whether it keeps earning that is a design call, not an operator one, and it is now sitting in front of Nathan with a price attached.

NOTHING HERE LICENSES RAISING CENSUS_REFUSAL_SECS. The test asks for three things and this supplies one and a half: attribution yes, optimisable share yes, condition for ratcheting back down NOT established. A ceiling raised without that third piece is the drift the ceiling exists to catch.
